newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-HEALY CRITICISES HIMSELF FOR SHOW OF DISSENT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HEALY CRITICISES HIMSELF FOR SHOW OF DISSENT.

text.p: Australia wicketkeeper and vice-captain Ian Healy has criticised himself after being banned for two matches for dissent while on tour in South Africa, Australian newspapers reported on Wednesday.
Healy was suspended by International Cricket Council match referee Raman Subba Row for throwing his bat after being dismissed in the third test against South Africa on Monday.

"I am extremely disappointed on two fronts that I have had to appear before the match referee after making a conscious effort for a number of years not to do so," Healy said in a statement released to reporters in South Africa.
"Firstly, that I lost my composure in a situation I should have been able to tolerate," Healy said.

"I have always been happy to be judged by the high standards and expectations of myself, my peers, and the public alike and certainly do not condone in any way my actions in throwing the bat," he said.
"Secondly I am unhappy to have allowed the many frustrations of the four days of the test to hit so hard," said Healy.
Healy, who was clearly incensed by the circumstances surrounding his dismissal in the second innings in Pretoria, will miss two limited overs internationals against South Africa this weekend.
The Queenslander glowered angrily with hand on hip at umpire Cyril Mitchley after he was adjudged caught behind down the legside during Australia's second innings.
Healy appeared to curse repeatedly as he walked to the pavilion before throwing his bat in front of him when he neared the dressing room.
Australia won the series 2-1 despite losing the third test convincingly.
